fact: The Government Communication Service statement points to free coding training for millions of young people as one of the government's investments preparing the new generation.

The Digital Ethiopia Skills and TVET in Action (DESTA) project, EUR 21m, launched with the Ministry of Labor and Skills, Germany, the EU and Finland, aims to equip youth with digital and entrepreneurial skills in five regions, per GIZ.

The Ministry of Education's CEO for ICT and Digital Education says a nationwide International Certification of Digital Literacy training initiative is running, with 64 certified trainers across 50 public universities and TVET institutions and Amharic and Afaan Oromo content underway.

The Ministry of Education's CEO says the nationwide International Certification of Digital Literacy initiative has equipped over 12,000 academic staff and nearly 200,000 students with digital skills and reached close to 3,000 community members.
Addis Fortune says Ethiopia announced on 27 July 2024, with the UAE government, a programme to give five million Ethiopians digital skills (five million coders).
The Public Procurement Service says the government's 5 Million Ethiopian Coders initiative was launched to give free digital training to five million citizens; no number trained nationally is given.
